log.why: Directly testing top candidate ompF (0.411 prior) can yield an immediate high-confidence confirmation or strongly point toward second-place lacZ.
Treating at 3 uM splits the posterior distribution nearly in half (0.656 vs 0.344), maximizing information gain for Ticket 2 while Ticket 1 incubates.
Testing lacZ directly splits the posterior evenly and can confirm the leading hypothesis.
E4 (10 µM) directly tests the leading hypothesis (0.472) and splits the posterior probability mass (~0.65 vs ~0.35).
The lacZ knockout lost the phenotype, giving a 0.929 posterior for lacZ, which is confident enough to publish now.
E4 splits Ticket 3's prior probability nearly in half (0.461 for <=10 µM vs 0.539 for >10 µM) and starts incubation early.
E5 tests the top two candidate genes (combined 0.581 posterior), efficiently bisecting the hypothesis space for Ticket 4.
With E3 negative and E4 positive, 10 µM has a strong 0.688 posterior; publishing now secures points and opens a slot for new tickets.
E3 at 3 µM cleanly splits the posterior mass between <=3 µM (0.477) and >=10 µM (0.523), potentially confirming 10 µM.
E8 tests {lacZ, fliC} (0.601 combined probability), isolating sodA if negative or narrowing to two candidates if positive.
Test 1 uM on expiring Ticket 3 to distinguish between 3 uM (0.497) and lower thresholds (0.394 total).
Directly tests lacZ to distinguish between the two remaining likely candidates, lacZ (0.521) and fliC (0.423), while waiting for Ticket 3.
Ticket 3 has only 4 seconds left and 3 uM has a strong 0.766 posterior after positive response at 3 uM and negative at 1 uM.
With only 17s remaining on Ticket 4, fliC has a strong 0.790 posterior, so we must publish before time expires.
Test {hisG, ftsZ} (0.444 total prior mass) to quickly narrow down the culprit gene on the expiring ticket.
Run E11 {hisG, recA, gyrA} in parallel with E6 {hisG, ftsZ} to quickly distinguish the top gene candidates.
With only 13 seconds left on Ticket 5 and 0.760 posterior on ftsZ, we must publish now before it expires.
Only 10 seconds remain in the round, which is not enough time to run an experiment and publish, and current posteriors have negative expected value.
